title: bus: push-verdict refuses a nonce unbound to its dispatch's head
body:
`bus.sh push-verdict` checked only that a `bus-nonce:` line was *present*; nothing
tied the nonce to a dispatch. On #2075 a reviewer whose head moved re-issued its
verdict with the nonce from the original dispatch at the old head: `push-verdict`
accepted it, the seat went idle, and only `confirm` refused -- a full extra round
trip to mint a fresh dispatch and re-publish the same verdict.

`push-verdict` now resolves the nonce in `$S/dispatched` before it proposes, and
refuses at publish time naming which of three facts failed -- unknown nonce;
another pull request's nonce; a nonce whose dispatch head is not the head the
verdict names -- each with a fresh `bus.sh dispatch` at that head as the remedy.
`confirm` keeps its check unchanged, so the publish gate and the signed gate
cannot diverge. `$S` is `$HPO_BUS_STATE` else `$HOME/.zcode/bus`, a per-machine
path; a seat is a subagent of the orchestrator's one session on one machine, so
`dispatch`, `push-verdict` and `confirm` resolve the same `$S` and the reviewer
sees the record its own brief named -- the header states that precondition and
what a reviewer on another machine sees.

The same PR records the process rule in `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md`
section 7 (policy, owner-approved): a head move that re-issues a verdict takes a
fresh `bus.sh dispatch` at the new head before the reviewer publishes. That
contract sat at zero headroom, so the rule raises its cap with the owner's
confirmation before the push, in `dev/governance/config/policy_budgets.json` --
a raise, not a quiet re-record. leaves #201 open.

## Head

`04a4705f062a977337aa7f703fed877b5b7315de` merges main `adc0ae5` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`4346950201e0ca6aa8d3b93a162b29abb3dde783` merges `origin/main` `595c23b57` into
the previous head `b80b76c01a` by hand. Two files conflicted and both were
resolved keeping both sides:

- `tools/audit/seat/bus.sh` -- one hunk, the self-test's `local` declarations:
  this branch's `N1c` (the fresh-dispatch-at-a-moved-head arm) and this branch's
  removal of `rs` (the stale-nonce arm now refuses at publish instead of
  proposing an undispatched verdict) together with main's `orphans`-arm locals
  (`o1 o2 u1 u2 c1 c2 s1 m1 mb`). No behaviour hunk conflicted: the nonce
  binding in `dispatch_binding`/`push_verdict` and main's `orphans`/
  `content_superseded` sit in disjoint regions.
- `dev/governance/config/policy_budgets.json` -- main raised the orchestrator
  contract's caps to its own measured 316 lines / 4462 tokens; this branch's
  addition re-applied on top of main's structure measures 319 lines / 4513
  tokens, and the caps here are those measured values, so the raise over main
  is exactly the three lines the rule adds.

`dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` auto-merged cleanly and was read as an
artifact: main's section 5b (`orphans` dispatch rule) and section 6 wording sit
intact, and the branch's fresh-dispatch sentence is re-applied in section 7 in
its place.

`d240ff73d16e39f113b0527ee077076cc7e9a201`, one commit on top of
`78a06754145c1e0795629379fe5635edcffa3c4b` that adds only this PR's own row,
`dev/programme/delivery/2115.md`. `78a067541` is the merge of `origin/main`
`c729bb32e` into the authored head `6f220a553`.

## Mutation proof

`tools/audit/seat/bus.sh` is INERT, so no closure selects it; CI's `governance`
job runs its self-test directly, and the refusal arms below are that proof.
Driving the pre-fix script (`git show $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD):tools/audit/seat/bus.sh`)
and this head over one bare repository with a real `dispatch`:

```
arm                           pre-fix    fixed
unknown nonce                 ACCEPTED   REFUSED
another pull request's nonce  ACCEPTED   REFUSED
nonce at a moved head         ACCEPTED   REFUSED
correctly bound (control)     ACCEPTED   ACCEPTED
```

Removing the `why=$(dispatch_binding ...)` call restores all three ACCEPTED arms.
`bus.sh --self-test` carries one arm per refusal class plus the control.

## Null control

The unmodified tree accepts all three malformed verdicts and the correctly-bound
one (the pre-fix column above); the fixed tree refuses the three and still accepts
the control.

## Figures

- `bash tools/audit/seat/bus.sh --self-test` -- 56 checks, 0 failed, at this
  head, including the branch's refusal arms (`push-verdict refuses a nonce no
  dispatch minted`, `refuses another pull request's nonce`, `round 1's nonce
  does not count at another head`, the control `proposes a verdict its own
  dispatch minted the nonce for`) and main's `orphans` arms, so the merge kept
  both self-tests whole.
- `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` -- exit 0; the raised caps
  (319 lines, 4513 tokens) equal what the check measures for
  `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` at this head, and `corpus_tokens`
  stays inside its band.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)
  --workdir $(mktemp -d)` -- `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run`: `bus.sh` is
  INERT and no changed file is in a measured closure.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` -- STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED at this head.

## Red checks

- `budget-raise-gate` is red at this head by design: it reads the two raises in
  `dev/governance/config/policy_budgets.json` (the orchestrator contract's line
  cap and token cap, each moved to the value `--budgets` measures) and stays red
  until tvofi's approving review at this head, which it requires before it
  passes. It is the raise's own gate and the only detector that reads a raise, so
  no cheaper detector exists to answer with.

`fast (3.14)` — red in this head's history from two main-data defects, neither caused by this diff: (1) the closures lane-balance pole (boost_drift_replay.py recorded 3379.1 s > half the table since the 282054566 re-record), fixed by #2173's optimality arm and honest re-record; (2) the ci-budget row archscore.coord_footprint grown 2587->2592 by #2118 without re-recording, fixed by #2175's deliberate re-record. Both landed before this head's recarry; the cheaper detector for each is the check that went red (the closure selftest pin, the entities null control) — no additional standing detector is warranted.

`closures` — red once at the pre-recarry head from the composed-verify stdout leak (`cp: cannot stat .../composed/composed-verify:.json`: a foreign token from composed-verify's output entered the consume loop's file list), fixed on main by #2164's stdout contract (diagnostics to stderr); the recarry that produced this head consumes that fix. The cheaper detector is the consume loop itself failing loudly — which is exactly how this surfaced; standing cost is one failed lane per leak, removed by the contract.

`closures-autofix` — red once in this branch's history from the same family the recarry consumed: the pre-#2164 composed-verify stdout leak era's downstream artifact failure (the lane's repair never ran because the recording it consumes never landed — "Artifact not found: closure-recordings") and the stale-table failures before #2173 landed. Not caused by this diff; the cheaper detector is the lane itself, which re-fires on every push and names a real closure defect.

`arch-score` and `env-matrix` — red in this branch's history (22:1x-22:4xZ window) on the GitHub App installation's exhausted hourly API quota (HTTP 403 inside the jobs before any scoring/matrix ran): infra failures, not defects of this diff; both checks re-fire on every pull_request event and have run green in this window elsewhere. The cheaper detector is each check itself.

`validate-hacs` — red in this branch's history during the 22:1x-22:4xZ window when the GitHub App installation's hourly API quota was exhausted (HTTP 403 in the job): an infra failure, not a defect of this diff; the check re-fires on every pull_request event and validates the integration manifest identically each time.
## Forward-carry

`dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` section 7 -- the fresh-dispatch rule,
landed in this PR.

## Approval

Policy: `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` (a new rule) and its cap raise in
`dev/governance/config/policy_budgets.json`. The owner confirmed both in this
session before the push: include the process rule in this PR, and raise the
contract's cap to the value `--budgets` measures. This PR merges only on tvofi's
approving GitHub review at its head -- `budget_raise_gate.py` accepts an approval
only at the head, so the review must name that head.

## Friction

none.
